The graph above shows the function $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡(Bx)+D,$ where $B$ and $D$ are constants. What is $D-B?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The period $T$ of the function is

$$
T=\frac{3\pi }{4}-(-\frac{3\pi }{4})=\frac{6\pi }{4}=\frac{3\pi }{2}.
$$

The formula for the period $T$ of the function $y=A\operatorname{tan}⁡(Bx+C)+D$ is given by 

$$
T=\frac{\pi }{B}.
$$

Applying the formula of the period, we get

$$
\frac{3\pi }{2}=\frac{\pi }{B}\,⟹\,B=\frac{\pi }{(\frac{3\pi }{2})}=\frac{2}{3}.
$$

The parameter $D$ represents the vertical shift of the tangent function. We see that the function has been translated by $1$ units up. Hence, $D=1.$

Therefore, $D-B=1-(\frac{2}{3})=\frac{1}{3}.$

Finally, the equation of the curve is

$$
y=\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{2x}{3})+1.
$$
